newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo palladium ends sharply higher on NY gains.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo palladium ends sharply higher on NY gains.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo palladium futures ended sharply higher on Wednesday, with the October and December contract rising by their daily 22 yen limit, reflecting an overnight rally in New York, traders said.
Limitless spot July ended up 48 yen at 730 yen per gram, and benchmark June 1998 ended 14 yen higher at 564 yen.
Active buying from individual investors, encouraged by the rally in New York, emerged from the opening, traders said.
But traders said the rise in Tokyo was smaller than they had expected. "I had expected all contracts to rise by their daily limit today," a trader at a major trade house said.
Platinum futures ended mixed, and benchmark June closed down 10 yen at 1,365 yen per gram.
Traders said they were still waiting for Russian platinum to arrive. "We've received no notice at this stage," said a senior official of a major bullion house.
Russia's platinum group metal export agency, Almazjuvelirexport, has said it would resume exports this week.

Traders said that platinum supplies in Japan were not as tight as palladium. "We're asking Russia to ship platinum supplies as soon as possible. But the situation is not as critical as palladium," a trader said.
Yen-based gold futures closed weaker. Prices ranged from 11 to 16 yen lower, with benchmark June 1998 finishing down 13 yen at 1,188 yen per gram.
Bullion was quoted $323.75/324.15 per ounce at 0810 GMT, down compared with $325.30/80 in New York overnight.
Silver futures ranged from unchanged to 1.7 yen per 10 grams lower. Benchmark June was down 0.6 yen at 162.7 yen.
